blocks.text: Cut a slice from a round loaf of Agege bread and you have made a sector. The crust along the outside is the arc. Everything in this subtopic comes from one question: what fraction of the whole circle is your slice?

blocks.markdown:
A **sector** is the region bounded by two radii and an arc. The angle between the radii, $\theta$, is the angle at the centre.

A full turn is $360°$, so a sector of angle $\theta$ is exactly $\dfrac{\theta}{360}$ of the whole circle. Every formula below is just the whole-circle formula multiplied by that fraction.

blocks.caption: The same fraction, θ/360, applies to both circumference and area

blocks.title: One idea, two formulas
blocks.text: You do not need to memorise two separate formulas. Work out the fraction $\frac{\theta}{360}$ first, then multiply it by the circumference for an arc or by the area for a sector area. A $90°$ sector is a quarter circle; a $60°$ sector is one sixth.

blocks.title: Arc length and sector area together
blocks.prompt: A sector of a circle of radius 21 cm has an angle of 60° at the centre. Find its arc length and its area. Take π = 22/7.

steps.text: Find the fraction of the circle.
Take one sixth of it for the arc length.
Take one sixth of that for the sector area.

blocks.answer: Arc length 22 cm; sector area 231 cm²

blocks.markdown:
### Perimeter of a sector

The perimeter of a sector is **not** just the arc. You must walk all the way round the boundary, which means along one radius, round the arc, and back along the other radius:

$$\text{perimeter of sector} = \text{arc length} + 2r$$

For a $90°$ sector of radius 14 cm, the arc is $\frac{1}{4} \times 88 = 22$ cm, so the perimeter is $22 + 28 = 50$ cm.

blocks.caption: Recognising these fractions makes the arithmetic much faster

blocks.markdown:
### Working backwards

Exam questions often give the arc length or the sector area and ask for the angle or the radius. Set up the same equation and solve it.

If a sector of radius 14 cm has area $154$ cm², then the whole circle has area $616$ cm², so the fraction is $\frac{154}{616} = \frac{1}{4}$, and the angle is $\frac{1}{4} \times 360 = 90°$.

blocks.title: Folding a sector into a cone
blocks.text: When a sector is folded into a cone, the **arc becomes the base circumference** and the **radius of the sector becomes the slant height** of the cone. So for a sector of radius 5 cm and angle $216°$: the arc is $\frac{216}{360} \times 10\pi = 6\pi$, and setting $2\pi r = 6\pi$ gives a base radius of 3 cm.

points: A sector of angle $\theta$ is $\frac{\theta}{360}$ of the whole circle.
Arc length is that fraction of the circumference; sector area is that fraction of the area.
The perimeter of a sector includes the two radii as well as the arc.
To find an unknown angle or radius, form the same equation and solve it.
When a sector is folded into a cone, the arc becomes the base circumference and the sector radius becomes the slant height.
